result: M16 PASS at c5292f7. reports/platform/PLT01-STEPRATE/timefidelity.json. Exit code 0, checked directly and not through a pipeline.

findings.headline: The brief and S39 both say nothing reads the counters. Half true, and the true half is worse than stated.
findings.detail: catchupClamps IS exposed (engine.js:7887) and HAS been read twice as narrative (W1-00, W1-01-province-stream-r1). catchupDroppedMs was exposed NOWHERE — the running world could report that world time had been thrown away and never how much. What was actually missing in both cases is a THRESHOLD: no item stated a number either had to meet, which is observationally identical to not counting at all. Demonstrated: the `nocount` null control (stop incrementing catchupDroppedMs) scores a perfect 1.0000 fidelity at 2.32 Hz while the world still runs at a fifth speed.

findings.headline: 19.3% is now a derivation, not a SwiftShader anecdote.
findings.detail: world_time_fidelity = min(1, MAX_CATCHUP x STEP_MS x raf_hz / 1000), verified exactly at eleven swept rates by driving the SHIPPED FixedLoop from Node with a synthetic clock and synthetic rAF. Needs no browser, no GPU, and gives the same answer on a phone as on SwiftShader — RI-PLT01 Tier-S in the strong sense. 2.32 Hz -> 0.193333, steps_per_raf exactly 5.000, clamp_run 400 of 400.

findings.headline: S39's 'the fight stays fair AND READABLE' — fair is upheld, readable is not.
findings.detail: Uniform stretch preserves every ratio between two SIMULATED quantities. images_per_sim_frame = rendersTotal/simStepsTotal is a simulated quantity over a RENDERED one and is not preserved: below the floor the loop runs 5 steps per rAF and draws once, so it falls to 0.2. roll.json LIGHT ships iframe_count 26; the player is shown ~5 pictures of that window instead of ~26, and an 18-frame RI-AI02 telegraph becomes 3.6 pictures. That is verbatim RI-PLT01's founding argument. Filed as P13, whose numbers are C.1's own 40/55 fps floors divided by 60. Does NOT move where the defect is scored; does mean a critic may not cite S39 to argue a slow device is merely slow. Reversible: strike P13 if a hands-on judgement ever calls the fight readable below 0.67.

findings.headline: Two floors, and they are different numbers. S39's 12.00 Hz is right; the per-tick threshold is 10.00 Hz.
findings.detail: A single tick clamps iff arrears reach (MAX_CATCHUP+1) x STEP_MS = 100 ms = 10.00 Hz. A SUSTAINED rate keeps real time only at/above MAX_CATCHUP x STEP_MS = 12.00 Hz, because residues accumulate and the clamp that eventually fires ZEROES the accumulator. Measured at 11.5 Hz: fidelity 0.9583 with one clamp. A builder who checks the per-tick figure writes a check that passes at 11.5 Hz.

findings.headline: 12.00 Hz is a cliff edge, not a safe place to sit.
findings.detail: STEP_MS = 1000/60 is not representable in binary; at exactly 12.00 Hz arrears come to 99.9999999999999 against a nominal 100 and whether a tick clamps is decided in the last bits of a double. Measured over 400 ticks (33.3 s): one clamp, fidelity 0.9990 — on the line of P10's session bound.

findings.headline: The 11.6 steps/s headline is a SwiftShader number and may not be reported as a fact about a phone.
findings.detail: critic-gate-wallclock.json (fa96455) and reports/w1-touch-r2/framerate.json were both taken in this container on a shared box. Under RI-PLT01 T1 those are Tier-H quantities; 'a phone at 11.6 steps/s' is the inference 'How we lose' #5 exists to forbid, and it has propagated into S39 and NEXT-DISPATCH §U. P10-P13 are marked Tier-H and score 0 here for exactly that reason. What survives with no device is the conditional, which is P14 and is proved.

null_controls.method: Four mutants of the SHIPPED loop.js, each a single-line edit, written to the scratchpad (never into game/src — RULES 17), guards import rewritten to an absolute URL so they share the process clock. Each asserts its anchor text matched, so an edit that did not apply throws rather than passing as an inert control.
null_controls.leak: RED — clamp branch stops zeroing the accumulator; spiral, fidelity -160.7
null_controls.nocount: RED — catchupDroppedMs stops incrementing; fidelity reads a perfect 1.0000 while the world runs at a fifth speed
null_controls.rafsteps: RED — rafDrivesSim true in every mode; P15 goes red, HF10's shape
null_controls.maxcatchup50: RED — MAX_CATCHUP 5->50 moves fidelity at 2.32 Hz from 0.1933 to 1.0000, establishing the cap as the cause
null_controls.inert_control_found_and_reported: maxcatchup50 came out GREEN on run 1 and is reported rather than quietly repaired: `predicted` is computed from the module's own MAX_CATCHUP, so the law self-adjusted and both arms were identical. That is RULES 6's inert control AND a true statement about the law — it cannot detect a change to MAX_CATCHUP, because the constant is on both sides. R3/M8 own that constant and do catch it. The control kept the mutation and changed what it is a control FOR: the headline number.

instrument_defects_in_my_own_tool_found_: Run 1: fidelity defined as simStepsTotal x STEP_MS / wall carried a window-boundary artefact (up to STEP_MS pending in the accumulator) and produced a FALSE FAIL at 12.00 Hz. Redefined on the counter: 1 - catchupDroppedMs/wall.
Run 2: the clamp iff asserted a closed form (arrears >= 6 x STEP_MS) against a machine not doing real arithmetic; 1-ULP false violations at 12.00 Hz. Now evaluated in the loop's own float order.

Run 3: the checker used the NOMINAL rAF period instead of the dt the loop actually computed; a clock advanced by 60 nominal steps reads back 16.666666666666629 on the first tick, below STEP_MS, running zero steps. Three phantom violations at 60 Hz. Now reads loop.lastWallMs.
not_done: PRIORITY 2 (why the step rate collapses at a handheld profile) was NOT re-measured by me, deliberately. W1-TOUCH-r2 is live and had already answered it better than the brief assumed: findings A1-A5 in orchestration/status/W1-TOUCH-r2.json, artifact reports/w1-touch-r2/framerate.json. Its answer: it does NOT collapse at the handheld profile — it collapses in play mode at EVERY profile and the handheld one was the fastest of three; the mechanism is the render (setRenderRate(0) moves rAF 1-2 Hz -> 24-25 Hz, a 16-25x move), not the touch overlay (no movement outside noise) and not dpr (+27%, real, small, not the cause). Re-running its sweep would have duplicated a live neighbour and paid its 67% load-noise tax again. My contribution is the load-INDEPENDENT half: the same mechanism as exact arithmetic, which needs no box at all.
P10-P13 and M17 are Tier-H and score `unmeasurable` = 0 until a run manifest attests real hardware. No device exists in this project. That is the item's design, not a gap I left.
No browser was launched. contention.mjs said GO; it was not needed, which is the point of M16.

MAX_CATCHUP — R3 fixes it at 5 and it is a binding number in a reference item, not a knob this piece may turn. Whether 5 is right is R3's question and is still open.
